taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and native to Texas at state scale.
look_here_first: Go directly to a mature LEAF SHEATH. Look for conspicuous long hairs along the sheath surface and margins, not only at the mouth; follow up with hairy sheath-throat and prominent hairs in some panicle branch axils. The open panicle resembles several other lovegrasses and cannot finish the ID alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Uvalde is the only exact project target-zone county currently locked. Statewide Texas nativity and the old Hays-local flag are not county proof.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is independent from native-range certification.

best_field_traits: ciliate sheath mouth and hairy ligule
morphology_keys.comparison_training: E. intermedia is much more glabrous on the sheaths; E. trichodes concentrates hairs near the sheath apex rather than across the sheath surface.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against plains and sand lovegrass, prioritize hairs along the hirsuta sheath BODY and margins, not merely a collar tuft. Both comparison species may have collar hairs and some panicle-axil pubescence. A truly shaggy sheath plus bearded branch axils supports E. hirsuta, but old/worn vegetation and variation can reduce the difference.

field_id_finish_pass.looked_at: Three preinstalled credited local photographs visually inspected 2026-10-20. Image 1 clearly resolves long sheath-surface hairs and hair tufts at a blade junction; image 2 shows fine panicle branches/spikelets; image 3 shows a partial flowering structure, not an entire mature panicle.
field_id_finish_pass.crew_summary: This is the hair-check lovegrass. Have crew run a finger and 10× lens along the SHEATH surface; contrast with plains lovegrass before ever using the airy seedhead as proof.
lookalike_logic: Plains: can have hairs around collar and lower panicle branch junctions, but usually not the same overall conspicuously hairy sheath body.
Sand: long tufts concentrated near sheath mouth; stem nodes generally glabrous.
Purple: very spread-out showy flower cloud; do not use purple color.
Witchgrass: spikelets need inspection to distinguish genera.
difficult_id_guardrails: The inspected sheath-hair photo does not show a measured ligule or a complete reproductive branch axil.
Kew/GrassBase says hirsute sheaths; regional FNA descriptions note hairiness can vary and be concentrated on distal margins; avoid an absolute 'every sheath fully hairy' rule.
County-native range is UNRESOLVED in canonical taxon; statewide Texas nativity does not certify user-zone PASS.
Source photo observations establish provisional image identity, not an independent expert specimen confirmation.
field_id_finish_pass.publish_check: Canonical visual lesson written and reviewed for structural arrow placement. Exact publishing and media gate remain independent.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Bigtop lovegrass: inspect the sheath BODY, not just the fluffy head
steps: Find a green leaf SHEATH along the culm and look for abundant hairs growing off the sheath surface/margins. The first annotated photograph really shows these.
Follow that sheath up to the blade junction and collar hair tuft. Avoid calling the fine leaves themselves ligules.
Move to a lower branch junction on the inflorescence; hairy axils support the ID but still need a dedicated macro photograph.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Hirsute sheaths plus hairy panicle branch axils strongly support bigtop; a solitary airy panicle photograph doesn't.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Arrowed hairs are visible, but the exact ligule, measured spikelet and bearded lower panicle branch axil are NOT verified in these images.

visual_comparison.title: Bigtop lovegrass — hairs are the first character
visual_comparison.subtitle: The existing first photo clearly shows actual long hairs on grass sheaths and at the leaf attachment. Source plant ID is recorded by GBIF and retained as provisional; arrows were inspected against the photograph.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: SHEATH HAIRS are more diagnostic than PURPLE PANICLE color.
